items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: I was named after my dad because my dad is an Isidore.

ctx.x: And who were you named after?
Well, I was named after my dad because my dad is an Isidore. Isidore. No, that is Isidore. John Barberin.
Is that J-O-H-N or J-E-A-N, John? J-O-H-N.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: They had Vic Gasper on baritone, my daddy on alto.

ctx.x: They don't have no musicians. No, shame on them.

You should hear those bands in those days, like the Olympia band, Superior band, and Imperial band, those was bands. And the parade, does he like the Armand Brass band? I mean, well, the Armand Brass band, I mean, they played my father, I mean, he can't tell you about that, because you didn't ask him about that. But I can tell you, they played ball house music. You can forget about what he said about the other fellas, you know, reading at that time. Yeah, but later on in the years, I mean, it was a Ball House…
Who were the Ball House men in that band?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: My father happened to be in that band at the time, and my father played the Conet at that time, an Armored Band.

ctx.x: Well, my uncle, my mother's brother, he was one of the finest clarinetists we had here in New Orleans, I understand. What I was told from a lot of old time musicians, his name was Louis Arthedale, and he played with the Armored Brass Band, it was many, many years ago. My father happened to be in that band at the time, and my father played the Conet at that time, an Armored Band. They played the Ford and Moist Parade, they played the Fireman's Parade, all big parades, played with a lot of bands. Who was Lincoln in…

It wasn't Manuel Perez in those days, somebody before then? No, no, before Manuel Perez's time, I wanted to know. That's what I wanted to make sure. He played the Coronet at first, then what did he play?

items.title: Isidore Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: But they never defined the bullet. He still had that bullet. Paul wasn't born yet.

ctx.x: Castor in the restaurant. And I got a stray bullet. There was three of us got... Wait.

The stomach. He stayed in the hospital. My mother was pregnant for him. He wasn't born yet. And he stayed in the hospital, I think my mother said 17 or 18 days. But they never defined the bullet. He still had that bullet. Paul wasn't born yet.
Can you ask him what a hoop drill was?
